newsitem.title: UK: British royal family holds meeting on future.
newsitem.headline: British royal family holds meeting on future.

text.p: Britain's royal family, buffeted by scandal and divorce, met on Sunday to try to restore its tarnished image.

Senior advisers said Queen Elizabeth's divorced sons Prince Charles and the Duke of York flew to Scotland for a family "board meeting" at Balmoral Castle of the 1,000-year-old monarchy whose popularity has plummeted.

Sweeping changes are up for discussion by the queen and her family over the next two days in the informally titled "Way Ahead Group," set up in 1992 after royal marriages started to fall apart and Windsor Castle was struck by a fire.
The monarch's historical role as the head of the Church of England could end, allowing heirs to the throne to marry Roman Catholics.
The ban on marrying Catholics was enshrined in 1701 to stop Papal interference in English life but it does not apply to any other religion and is now seen as offensive.

The Queen and her advisers have been looking at a choice of options aimed at ensuring the monarchy's survival into the 21st century. She has set up a strategic policy committee to review what changes could best be made.
The royal family might also be streamlined, cutting out cousins and other distant relatives widely seen as expensive appendages living off taxpayers' money.

The queen, one of the world's richest women with a personal fortune of 158 million pounds ($244 million), has already sought to counter criticism by offering in 1992 to pay income tax for the first time.
The marriage of heir-to-the-throne Charles and Princess Diana, launched amid pomp and pageantry 15 years ago, ended last month with a rubber-stamp divorce in the back office of a London court.

Their incompatibility and Charles's continuing love for Camilla Parker Bowles pushed Diana into attempting suicide. The glare of the media spotlight ruined any chance of reconciliation and they separated in 1992.

The divorce left Diana one of the most eligible women in the world but Charles faces anguish over his 26-year-long relationship with Parker Bowles, whom many Britons blame for the breakdown of the marriage.
Parker Bowles has been quoted as saying she will not marry Charles because this could wreck his chances of becoming king.
The couple are reported as intending to discreetly continue their romance and the royal family wants to persuade Britons to accept this.
